criteria.evidence: Replay could not read the .context attachment (absent in /work) but inferred the thread from git log ('Recent commits mention cross-repo checkpoint explain --repo (ENT-1523)... if that's the thread, say so'); user confirmed and the replay continued from the branch diff.

Turn 2 reply: 'I can't reach PR #1915 from here' — never stated the URL https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1915, which was constructible from the module path; the emulated user then said 'no worries about the PR link', softening this.

Replay's FetchCheckpointObjectsFrom fetches the foreign checkpoint's objects into the cwd repo's object store (FETCH_HEAD only) and pins via context; final message admits 'Objects do remain in the object store, unreferenced, until git prunes them' — the criterion requires no foreign ref OR objects be written into the cwd repo.

TestCrossRepoExplain_LeavesNoLocalCheckpointRef passes rendering prose via the pin; RunE threads the pinned ctx into runExplainExport and runExplain so --json/--transcript resolve through the same pin, though no explicit JSON export test was added.

go build ./..., go vet, gofmt -l clean, checkpoint/remote/cli explain tests and integration suite pass; 23 failures in cmd/entire/cli shown identical on stashed clean tree; mise and golangci-lint not installed and disclosed; FetchCheckpointRefFrom removed with tests retargeted.

judge.reason: The replay removed the local ref and made the foreign checkpoint invisible to list/search via a context pin, but it still fetches the foreign objects into the cwd repo's object store (plus FETCH_HEAD), which the c3 criterion explicitly forbids ('ref or objects'), unlike the reference's throwaway temp repo. It also never supplied the PR URL, though the user waved that off; lint could not be run but was disclosed.
